oop.fragment: Oracle object types with attributes and methods written in PL/SQL
oop.why: Model entities that live in tables.
oop.useWhen: When ADTs beat pure relational rows.
oop.price: Object-relational mapping and method dispatch cost inside the engine.

decl.fragment: embedded SQL remains declarative; PL/SQL adds blocks around it

static.fragment: PL/SQL types aligned with SQL NUMBER/VARCHAR2 and anchored %TYPE
static.why: Avoid datatype conversion at the SQL boundary.
static.price: %TYPE still lags when the table changes under you without recompile discipline.

malloc.price: PGA/SGA and job queue processes are DBA territory.
malloc.reason: PL/SQL runs inside Oracle; heap and scheduling belong to the RDBMS, not a language-level malloc/thread API.
